# Independent audit: equal-volume surplus window and width-estimate gap

Read all five sections of `candidate 8407bedf6b42ff39` independently and ran its verifier: **PASS, 5,000 exact checks.** The theorem is restricted to exactly three positive-volume fibers with equal endpoint volumes and actual midpoint volume at most 11a/8. The later boxes falsify coverage by the stated estimates, not OC or either proposed center.

If the paired endpoint capture P<a, both residual bodies have positive volume. Their actual Minkowski midpoint lies in the residual middle halfspace, of volume at most (1-Gamma)m by ordinary Grünbaum at the true Minkowski centroid. For fixed residual sum 2a-P, concavity of the root minimizes its two-term sum at (a,a-P). This gives (3), with the case P>=a harmless. All residual threshold boundaries are null because the continuous normal is nonzero; proper, tangent and saturated cuts are covered.

For 1<=r<=11/8 the root x lies in [1/2,1), so raising 2x-1<=x^2 to the integer d is legitimate. The resulting quadratic residual bound is correct. Its difference from Gamma(2-r) is concave in r; the displayed endpoint comparison shows its smaller endpoint is delta_d. The polynomial in Gamma has the exact endpoint values 55/121 and 55/4 on [4/11,1/2], hence delta_d>=55/7744>0. The exponential-series bound and the upper Gamma<=1/2 also hold for d=1. For actual equal-length intervals the midpoint ratio is necessarily one, so there is no hidden one-dimensional body case in the nominal larger interval of r.

At g_M, each ambient halfspace with nonzero continuous normal has own captured volume at least Gamma m and the proved paired residual payment. A purely integer halfspace through the source contains K and one endpoint, so its mass is at least 2a>c_d a; boundary mass is retained. Both g_M and g_K are actual middle-fiber points. The two deterministic raw guarantees c_d a and Gamma k have their unique ratio crossing at k/a=c_d/Gamma, which proves exactly eta_d=Gamma c_d/(c_d+2Gamma)>Gamma/2. Midpoint containment also proves that the lifted convex hull has exactly the three claimed fibers.

The directional support-distance estimate follows from the projected CDF bound F(s)>=s^d and integration of its complement. Supporting-point homotheties then give the actual cap-height bounds; clamping negative heights only strengthens the retained weighted-height inequality. If a height reaches a full width, the captured volume already exceeds the stated lower bound. Hölder gives (8) for d>1. Sectional Brunn--Minkowski and Fubini give (9) for d>=2, with all coarea factors accounted for by the same fixed direction. The discard of higher mixed section terms is explicitly acknowledged. The source's width section is read in this d>1 scope; formula (9) is not an all-d statement when d=1.

For the actual boxes, both endpoint volumes equal one and the midpoint volume is 9409/5184. In the first direction the true widths are both one. The d=3 residual quantity exceeds one exactly, and the stated deficit over W_3(1)=1/32 is 575/12288. Gamma_d decreases with d, while W_d(1) decreases and Gamma_d>1/3, so the exact comparison persists for every d>=3. At k=2 the actual centrally symmetric K has all continuous halfspace masses through its center equal to one, exceeding the raw OC target 2Gamma_d; purely integer cuts are harmless. Thus the estimate-bundle obstruction is realized, while the bodies explicitly satisfy OC as claimed.
